extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: FLEURS: Few-shot Leaming Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech benchmark
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.publisher: Meta AI Research, Google Research, Camegie Mellon University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process is simple. We start with the FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators. For each sentence in the 102 languages, we collected three recordings by three different native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: About 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Plan to fill gaps in future versions of the dataset
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded. All recordings are kept as they are, either from quiet or noisy environment, without any data augmentations. The speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Source transcripts are produced by human translators from FLoRes-101. We maintain the English translated transcripts, which are useful for tasks such as multi-modal speech translation evaluations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three versions of the sentences are provided: the original raw transcript (SRC RAW), the preprocessed version (SRC NORM), and its character-based version (SRC CHAR), which should be used for ASR.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available via TFDS and Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include data generalization limits and quality issues.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation, and Retrieval.
